svg.text: KV compression: how 2 tokens become 1 cache entry (C2)
One C2 layer, one sequence · C1 skips the softmax and keeps one entry per token
D = 512 values per entry ca_state fp32 [slots, 7, 2, 512] entry: 288 B (FP4) or 528 B (FP8)
Per value: softmax of the 2 scores, then the weighted sum of the 2 latents. Then norm, RoPE, cast, store.
Steps 4-6 are one fused kernel (fused_norm_rope_hadamard_cast_store_kvcache). C1: step 1 has no Gate (bf16 [1, 512]) and step 3 is skipped.
Decode: where does the first token of a pair wait?
In ca_state, a ring of 7 slots per sequence. Each token writes slot position % 7 (example: positions 999..1005).
This step (positions 1000..1005) makes 3 entries, at the odd positions: (1000, 1001) → entry 500,
(1002, 1003) → entry 501, (1004, 1005) → entry 502. Position 999 is older; it paired with 998 in an earlier step.
Why 7 slots: the kernel asserts ring ≥ ratio + tokens per step − 1 = 2 + 6 − 1 = 7 (tilelang_ops/compress.py:98).
512 values plus scales, interleaved per token. FP4 is the HF loader default (use_fp4_sparse_kv = True).
Bars are not to scale. One block row per layer holds 128 // ratio entries: C1 = 128, C2 = 64 (cache_engine.py:452-453).
Simplified: one sequence, no context parallelism. The ring holds 7 slots only with the defaults (DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE = 5).
Prefill uses another kernel: it reads the first token of a pair from the ring when that token came in an earlier step.
